content.jointProblem: Can an AVL-based stop-arrival predictor, integrated into PassengerView, achieve absolute ETA errors of at most 90 seconds for at least 85% of displayed predictions across the three Romanian networks? The first experiment would audit a representative target-city extract and compare timetable-offset, state-space and GRU baselines on temporally held-out trips, explicitly testing transfer to DataBridge’s 10-second telemetry and peak-hour or disruption conditions.

rationale.text: Novaković has directly relevant experience estimating bus travel times from archived AVL using latent-state models.

sources.quote: This study develops a Kalman filter formulation that treats segment-level travel time as a latent state evolving according to a random-walk process

rationale.text: Her stop-level arrival prediction research provides a relevant neural baseline and identifies congestion-related weaknesses that this project must test.

sources.quote: Long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks are evaluated for predicting bus arrival times at individual stops 1 to 5 stops ahead
both models underperform during the evening peak on lines sharing a congested corridor

rationale.text: She has developed and cross-city validated AVL preprocessing methods, with Python implementations relevant to preparing the company's archive.

sources.quote: validated against a comparable archive from a partner city in Hungary.
The pipeline consists of six sequential stages: deduplication, map matching, speed filtering, stop-event reconstruction, trip identification, and running-time segmentation.
Code is provided as open-source Python modules.

rationale.text: Her cross-network transfer study offers a concrete starting point for testing adaptation, rather than assuming Novi Sad models generalise to Romanian operations.

sources.quote: This study investigates whether a GRU model pre-trained on five years of Novi Sad AVL data can be fine-tuned with limited data
network topology differences limit gains beyond approximately 8 weeks of fine-tuning data.

rationale.text: Her deployment-oriented project addresses lightweight retraining without GPUs, although its planned pilots do not establish production readiness.

sources.quote: The project develops lightweight Bayesian and neural network models that can be retrained nightly on a standard server
without requiring GPU hardware. Pilot deployments are planned in Novi Sad and one partner city.

constraints.text: Acceptance must use the contractual displayed-arrival accuracy criterion; segment MAE, RMSE or MAPE alone cannot establish compliance.

sources.quote: their contracts require displayed ETAs to be within 90 seconds of the bus's actual arrival at least 85 percent of the time.

constraints.text: Data preparation and evaluation must handle the PostgreSQL archive's scale and 10-second telemetry; weather-dependent features cannot assume an existing weather integration.

sources.quote: Since 2021 we have been collecting GPS pings from 340 buses every ten seconds through DataBridge AVL.
The raw data sits in a PostgreSQL time-series table — roughly 2.8 billion rows at this point
We do not have weather data integrated yet.

constraints.text: Serving and feed integration must fit the company's Java/Spring, on-premise container infrastructure and GTFS-Realtime interfaces; research code alone is insufficient.

sources.quote: Java 17 backend with Spring Boot microservices
Docker and Kubernetes on on-premise cluster in Subotica data centre
GTFS and GTFS-Realtime feed generation

constraints.text: The work plan must fit limited company staffing and include modelling knowledge transfer rather than relying on an existing in-house forecasting team.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one senior backend engineer and one domain specialist part-time to a collaborative project
We have one data engineer on staff who knows Python well but has no background in time-series modelling.

constraints.text: Historical-data access requires a signed agreement, and publication terms must reconcile company restrictions with the researcher's preference to publish anonymised results.

sources.quote: with access to our full historical AVL dataset and timetable logs under a signed data-sharing agreement.
She prefers collaborations where her group retains the right to publish anonymised results.

constraints.text: The implementation schedule must be reconciled before commitment: the company's stated approval expectation is in 2024, while the researcher notes capacity for one new collaboration in 2026.

sources.quote: The Romanian contracts have a twelve-month implementation window starting from go-live approval, which we expect in Q3 2024.
Workload is moderate; she can take on one new collaboration in 2026.

risks: Published results concern other networks, telemetry conditions and metrics. Neither segment errors nor stop-level MAPE demonstrate the Romanian display-level contractual target; the first target-city benchmark must test this transfer explicitly.

Peak congestion is a documented weakness of the researcher's recurrent models, and her extreme-weather study reports degraded coverage early in snow events. Missing weather integration and unconfirmed disruption labels could limit robustness.

The approximately 2.8-billion-row company archive is substantially larger than the cited preprocessing validation archives. Extraction, reconstruction and retraining throughput remain unvalidated at this scale.

The historical company timetable may not align with the researcher's 2026 capacity. Joint-project willingness is open, but current availability and whether the single collaboration slot remains free are unknown.

Romanian-city historical coverage, arrival-ground-truth quality, serving hardware capacity, budget and operational ownership are unspecified. Gaps could prevent a valid benchmark or maintainable deployment.
Data-sharing or publication restrictions could block access or conflict with the researcher's publication preference.
questions: What are the actual approval date, current contractual deadline and status of the mid-2025 PassengerView release? Is Novaković's 2026 collaboration slot still available, and with what staffing and time commitment?
How is the 85% requirement calculated: prediction horizon, sampling frequency, per-city or pooled aggregation, exclusions, and treatment of cancellations, missing telemetry and stale displays?
Does the archive contain sufficient historical data for each Romanian network, including route variants, timetable versions and reliable stop-arrival ground truth from door events or another source?

Can the first experiment use representative peak, off-peak, roadworks and adverse-weather periods with chronological holdouts, city-specific results and comparison against the current PassengerView baseline?
What on-premise CPU, memory and storage resources, serving latency, refresh rate and outage-fallback requirements must the predictor meet?
Can weather and disruption data be obtained and time-aligned, and which inputs will be available reliably at inference time?
What budget and engineering allocation cover extraction, model development, deployment, monitoring and post-project maintenance, and who owns each responsibility?
What data-access, retention, anonymisation, cross-border processing, IP and publication terms can the company and participating municipalities approve?
